headlines.article_text: Tesla Roadster reveal: What to know about the delayed EV Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Tesla revealed its next-generation Roadster from a SpaceX test site in Texas on Thursday. CEO Elon Musk first debuted the Roadster refresh concept in 2017 but Tesla has since missed every targeted delivery date. Tesla said the new Roadster, equipped with SpaceX thrusters, can accelerate from zero to 60 miles per hour in less than a second. In this article TSLA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Tesla unveils its long-delayed Roadster nearly a decade after first revealing a next-generation version of its original electric sports ​car, at a launch event in Waco, Texas, US, on October 15, 2026, in this still image taken from a handout video. Tesla | Via Reuters Tesla showed off its long-delayed next-generation Roadster on Thursday, almost a decade after Elon Musk's company started taking deposits for the electric sports car. The event was livestreamed from a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas, near Waco, starting at 7:55 p.m. local time, or 8:55 p.m. ET. In attendance along with Musk were design leader Franz von Holzhausen and Lars Moravy, vice president of vehicle engineering. "You're going to see some crazy stuff tonight," Musk said. "You're going to see the results of what happens when you have a collaboration with the world's best car company and the world's best rocket company." Tesla's original Roadster, designed and engineered by a team led by founding CEO Martin Eberhard, was based on a Lotus Elise chassis and was first delivered in 2008, selling for roughly $100,000 in small volumes until 2012. The next-generation Roadster is expected to be a high-end, low-volume model that relies on SpaceX technology to enable it to hover. While Musk fanatics expressed their excitement on social media, the Roadster isn't likely to have any material financial impact on the company. At the event, Musk and his team showcased a white sports car that raced up a curved ramp, then clung to it upside down and vaulted off it, flipping in mid-air and hovering slowly before landing on the ground. The two-seater can go from zero to 60 miles per hour in under a second, according to Tesla's timer, a feat Moravy demonstrated for the live audience. Musk said the next-generation Roadster would enter production in 2028. The price wasn't announced, and the company didn't disclose specifications about other performance-level variants of the new Roadster. Tesla reopened reservations for the refreshed Roadster in recent weeks, accepting $50,000 deposits from prospective buyers in the U.S., Canada and China. Musk first promoted the refreshed Roadster concept at an event in November 2017 , and the following June in a series of tweets. He wrote at that time, "SpaceX option package for new Tesla Roadster will include ~10 small rocket thrusters arranged seamlessly around car." The engines would improve speed and braking, and may "even allow a Tesla to fly." The prototype Tesla showed on Thursday is built to be as lightweight as possible with a steer-by-wire system, steering yoke, and an array of technologies developed by SpaceX, including thrusters, carbon overlay pressure vessels and diffusers, and powerful fans that enable the car to do some gymnastics. One feature Tesla left out of its forthcoming Roadster is the company's "FSD" or automated driving system. Musk said the new Roadster will be the last vehicle the company produces that's intended to be controlled by a human driver. watch now VIDEO 4:03 04:03 Dan Ives on Tesla stocks: A big step in the right direction Closing Bell Tesla started taking $50,000 deposits for the revamped Roadster in 2017, but has since missed every targeted delivery date. As recently as last October, Musk was hyping a Roadster demo that he hoped would happen before the end of 2025. That didn't take place either. Musk's former friend and OpenAI co-founder Sam Altman mocked the Tesla CEO in posts on X last year over the extreme delays, showing screenshots of his reservation and refund requests. "I really was excited for the car! And I understand delays," Altman wrote. "But 7.5 years has felt like a long time to wait." Altman got his refund, and the two ended up in court earlier this year over a separate matter related to OpenAI's governance and ownership structure. Others have kept their reservations. Lawrence O'Connor, founder and CEO of Other World Computing in Austin, Texas, told CNBC ahead of the event that he reserved a Founder's Edition of the new Roadster in November 2017, effectively giving the company what he called an "interest-free loan" of $250,000. O'Connor wrote in a message that he would be attending the show and was "excited to see what has been 9 years in the making." After the event, O'Connor said what he saw was "off the charts." Tesla is scheduled to report third-quarter results after the bell on Wednesday. Eric Thayer | Los Angeles Times | Getty Images SpaceX artificial intelligence policy leader Gabriela Castillo Madrid is set to testify before the New York City Council on Friday as part of a legislative investigation into AI safety. The hearing with the council's tech committee is scheduled for 10 a.m. ET at City Hall with Castillo Madrid appearing by video conference. Elon Musk's aerospace, defense tech and AI company originally evaded requests and a subpoena from the city council to appear alongside leaders from OpenAI , Anthropic , Google and Meta on Oct. 5. SpaceX agreed to testify earlier this week after the council threatened to have its subpoena enforced by a judge. The council opened its probe following a month of intense debate surrounding the risks posed by advanced AI models, and is aiming to use testimony and information unearthed through the investigation to guide new regulations. Before Castillo Madrid took a role in government affairs at SpaceX earlier this year, she worked at X, Musk's social media company that's now owned by SpaceX, according to her LinkedIn profile . Prior to that, she spent almost three years at the U.S. Department of Commerce. In merging SpaceX with xAI in February, Musk combined his AI and social networking business with his rocket launch company, which also owns the Starlink satellite internet service. The merger put SpaceX in control of AI model Grok, which is used by some federal agencies, including the Pentagon . SpaceX went public in June and is now valued at about $2 trillion. In August, SpaceX completed a $60 billion acquisition of AI coding startup Cursor. In skipping the earlier NYC Council hearing, SpaceX avoided direct questioning from a member of the U.K. Parliament, Jess Asato, who testified about experiencing AI-enabled online harassment. Asato is suing xAI in the U.K. after Grok users created and distributed sexualized images of her online without her consent. She's seeking damages, alleging misuse of her private information and breaches of European data protection rules. According to the BBC , Asato criticized SpaceX for its "arrogance" in not appearing last week. SpaceX didn't respond to a request for comment ahead of the meeting. headlines.article_text: Marco Rubio to visit Reliance refinery in Jamnagar, India Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Rubio will visit the world's largest oil refinery in Jamnagar, owned by Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani's firm Reliance Industries. The Trump administration has been trying to ease diesel prices, which affect American truckers, farmers, and shippers, ahead of the midterm polls. Ambani is developing strong ties with the Trump administration by investing in the first new refinery project in the U.S. in 50 years and buying more Venezuelan oil barrels. EVIAN-LES-BAINS, FRANCE - JUNE 17: (LtoR) US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor attend a bilateral meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the G7 Summit on June 17, 2026 in Evian-les-Bains, France. Anna Moneymaker | Getty Images News | Getty Images U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is set to visit the world's largest oil refinery in Jamnagar, India, owned by billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries , as diesel prices surge ahead of U.S. midterm polls. The International Energy Agency has warned that constraints on the diesel market will likely keep prices elevated into the next year. To ease diesel prices, which affect American truckers, farmers, and shippers, U.S. President Donald Trump earlier this month paused sanctions on Russia to allow supplies from Moscow in the global market. The Trump administration is using this trip to focus on business deals rather than policy and politics as Americans remain focused on the economy ahead of the midterm polls, experts told CNBC. Not only is Ambani's flagship company Reliance investing in a U.S. refinery and is a key buyer of Venezuelan oil, but its strong ability to supply diesel has put Jamnagar on the map during Rubio's visit, they added. On Tuesday, the U.S. Department of State announced that Rubio will be traveling to Samarkand in Uzbekistan and from there to Mumbai and Jamnagar in India , with no mention of a stop in New Delhi, between Oct. 17 and 22. Rubio, who is on his second trip to India this year, will meet with some senior Indian officials and with business leaders "to promote opportunities for commercial investment and economic cooperation," according to the release. U.S.-Ambani ties US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said Rubio will travel to Jamnagar to visit Reliance's refining complex and hinted that Ambani would meet the U.S. official , according to Bloomberg. Given Ambani runs Reliance, "I'd imagine he'd be there," Gor said, according to the report. Later in an interview with Indian media outlet NDTV, Gor said that the visit to Jamnagar was scheduled given Reliance's "incredible" investment in the U.S. refinery project. Reliance did not respond to emails sent by CNBC seeking details on the visit. The State Department did not respond to CNBC's queries sent outside of working hours. The U.S. is facing exceptionally high diesel prices ahead of its November midterm elections, and the Trump administration has been looking for ways to increase fuel availability, Arpit Chaturvedi, South Asia Advisor at strategic advisory firm Teneo, told CNBC. Jamnagar has "considerable export-oriented refining capacity," making a strong case for the U.S. to explore refined-product supplies, including diesel, he added. Ambani, who SpaceX founder Elon Musk referred to as the real boss of India last week, has been developing ties with the Trump administration. In March, U.S. President Donald Trump thanked Reliance for its " tremendous investment " in the first new refinery project in the U.S. in the last 50 years. Reliance, which is majority-owned by the Ambani family, has also emerged as the second-largest buyer of Venezuelan crude outside of the U.S ., even as Indian state-owned firms remain largely unmoved by Trump's appeal to buy more of it. Rubio will also use the visit to highlight "Reliance's plans for a large, new refinery in Texas, which is the site of heated midterm U.S. election races drawing national attention," said Atman Trivedi, a partner at Washington-based DGA Albright Stonebridge Group. Reliance's is also "well-positioned to sell diesel," and other refined petroleum products to the U.S., he added. The Jamnagar refinery is the world's " largest and most complex single-site refinery" with crude processing capacity of 1.4 million barrels per day, according to Reliance. It is a secure satellite network for government and national security users, built using Starlink technology and SpaceX launch capabilities. The service adds government-focused security, dedicated user equipment, and missions such as Earth observation and hosted payloads. Ukraine has accused SpaceX -owned Starlink of restricting its military-grade services , known as Starshield, as Russia intensified attacks on Kyiv. Officials in Kyiv said SpaceX had imposed restrictions on Starshield without advance notice, disrupting military operations and hampering efforts to protect civilians amid intense Russian attacks this week. In response, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk appeared to shift responsibility for any changes to Starshield's use in Ukraine to the U.S. government and President Donald Trump . He said that Starshield systems are owned and controlled by Washington, with the U.S. military and ultimately the president determining any limits on their use. The White House and the Pentagon didn't immediately reply to CNBC's request for comment. Here's what to know about Starshield, and how it differs from Starlink. What is Starshield and how does it work? Starshield is SpaceX's satellite network designed for government and national security use, building on the technology developed for Starlink. On Tuesday, Ukrainian officials reported that their Starlink communication systems were no longer working for terminals moving at speeds above 100 miles per hour, or about 160 kilometers per hour. Ukraine relies on this connectivity to track and intercept incoming threats.
